documents.title: Northline Desk: Lumenarc Dynamics Series D
Lumenarc Dynamics Announces Helios Array and $400 Million Series D
Harbor Brief: Lumenarc Dynamics Helios Array
VoltStreet Markets: Lumenarc Dynamics Series D

document_versions.content:
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE

Wire ID: LF-PR-2026-031

Red Mesa, Arizona — March 4, 2026 — Lumenarc Dynamics today announced the Helios Array, a planned network of compute campuses, and closed a $400 million Series D financing led by Northwind Capital.

The company said the Helios Array is planned to reach 1.8 GW of compute capacity by 2029.

The Helios Array's first campus is in Red Mesa, Arizona.

Chief Executive Officer Mara Ellison said the financing funds construction of that first campus.

This document is the original Lumenarc Dynamics announcement for wire ID LF-PR-2026-031.

Northline Desk — March 5, 2026

Lumenarc Dynamics has closed a $400 million Series D led by Northwind Capital, according to the company's March 4, 2026 press release (wire ID LF-PR-2026-031, https://lumenarc.example/press/2026-03-04-helios-array).

The release says the Helios Array is planned to reach 1.8 GW of compute capacity by 2029.

The release places the Helios Array's first campus in Red Mesa, Arizona.

Northline is republishing that Lumenarc Dynamics announcement and does not add a second primary financing document.

VoltStreet Markets — March 5, 2026

Lumenarc Dynamics closed a $480 million Series D led by Northwind Capital, according to the company's March 4, 2026 press release (wire ID LF-PR-2026-031, https://lumenarc.example/press/2026-03-04-helios-array).

The cited release says the Helios Array is planned to reach 1.8 GW by 2029.

The cited release places the Helios Array's first campus in Red Mesa, Arizona.

VoltStreet cites wire ID LF-PR-2026-031 and does not cite a second primary document.

Harbor Brief — March 6, 2026

A March 4, 2026 Lumenarc Dynamics announcement (https://lumenarc.example/press/2026-03-04-helios-array, wire ID LF-PR-2026-031) says the company closed a $400 million Series D financing led by Northwind Capital.

The announcement says the Helios Array is planned to reach 1.8 GW of compute capacity by 2029.

The announcement places the Helios Array's first campus in Red Mesa, Arizona.

Harbor Brief attributes the financing figures in this article to that single Lumenarc Dynamics press release.
